title: Race Course | Kolkata Trips
description: Discover Race Course Kolkata, home of the Royal Calcutta Turf Club. Learn about its history, architecture, entry details, best time to visit, visitor tips.
textContent: Race Course The Race Course Kolkata, officially managed by the Royal Calcutta Turf Club (RCTC), is one of India’s oldest and most prestigious horse racing venues. Located in the heart of Kolkata beside the sprawling Maidan, this historic racecourse has witnessed nearly two centuries of sporting excellence, royal patronage, and colonial history. Even if you are not visiting during a race meeting, the Race Course remains one of Kolkata’s most recognizable landmarks. Surrounded by lush greenery and iconic colonial-era buildings, it offers visitors a glimpse into the city’s British heritage while showcasing one of India’s oldest sporting traditions. For travelers exploring Kolkata, the Race Course is often included alongside the Victoria Memorial, St. Paul’s Cathedral, Fort William, and the Maidan, making it an essential stop on a heritage tour. Overview Feature Details Location Hastings, Kolkata, West Bengal Established 1820 Managed By Royal Calcutta Turf Club (RCTC) Famous For Horse racing Track Length Approximately 2,400 metres Best Known Event Calcutta Derby Stakes Nearby Landmark Victoria Memorial History of Race Course Kolkata The history of Race Course Kolkata dates back to 1820, making it one of the oldest racecourses in Asia. Horse racing was introduced during British rule when Kolkata (then Calcutta) served as the capital of British India. British officers, merchants, and aristocrats brought the sport from England, and it soon became one of the city’s most fashionable social events. The Royal Calcutta Turf Club (RCTC) was established in 1847 and rapidly gained international recognition. By the late nineteenth century, the club had become one of the most influential racing authorities in the world, regulating horse racing across India and several neighboring countries. The club received the prestigious “Royal” designation from the British Crown, reflecting its importance within the British Empire. For decades, members of Indian royalty, British governors, military officers, industrialists, and social elites gathered here to witness world-class horse racing. Architecture and Design The Race Course is much more than a sporting venue. Its expansive grounds cover hundreds of acres of beautifully maintained lawns, racing tracks, paddocks, and colonial-era structures. Architectural highlights include: Elegant colonial grandstands Historic members’ pavilion Traditional jockey weighing rooms Horse paddocks Viewing galleries Beautiful landscaped gardens Classic white railings surrounding the track The racecourse blends Victorian sporting architecture with expansive green spaces, creating one of Kolkata’s most scenic open areas. The Royal Calcutta Turf Club The Royal Calcutta Turf Club remains one of India’s most respected horse racing institutions. It organizes: Winter Racing Season Monsoon Racing Season Derby races Stakes races Classic horse racing events Equestrian activities The club continues to preserve centuries-old racing traditions while embracing modern race management. Horse Racing at Kolkata Race Course Horse racing generally takes place during the racing seasons. Visitors can experience: Thoroughbred horse racing Parade of horses Professional jockey competitions Live betting (where legally permitted) Grandstand viewing Food and beverage facilities Family-friendly atmosphere Major racing events attract enthusiasts from across India. Famous Races Some of the best-known races include: Calcutta Derby Stakes Calcutta Oaks Queen Elizabeth II Cup Monsoon Trophy Winter Championship races These prestigious competitions feature some of India’s finest thoroughbred horses. Flora and Green Spaces The Race Course is surrounded by the vast Maidan, often called the “Lungs of Kolkata.” Visitors enjoy views of: Mature banyan trees Palm-lined roads Expansive lawns Seasonal flowering plants Open green landscapes Numerous bird species The peaceful environment offers a refreshing contrast to Kolkata’s busy streets. Timings The Race Course is primarily open during scheduled racing days. Race Days Gates generally open several hours before the first race. Race schedules vary by season. Non-Race Days Public access may be restricted. Entry is generally limited to members, authorized visitors, or specific events. Visitors should check the official race calendar before planning their visit. Entry Fees Entry charges vary depending on: Race day Enclosure selected Special events Membership status Premium enclosures and members’ areas have separate access rules. Best Time to Visit The ideal time to visit is: October to March During these months: Pleasant weather Major racing events Comfortable sightseeing Clear skies Beautiful green surroundings Winter racing season offers the most exciting experience. How to Reach Race Course Kolkata By Metro The nearest metro stations include: Maidan Rabindra Sadan Esplanade From these stations, taxis and app-based cabs are easily available. By Taxi Yellow taxis, app-based cabs, and private vehicles can directly reach the Race Course. By Bus Several city buses operate along: Red Road Cathedral Road Jawaharlal Nehru Road By Train The nearest major railway stations are: Howrah Junction Sealdah Station Both are within a short driving distance. Nearby Attractions The Race Course is ideally located close to many of Kolkata’s iconic landmarks. Victoria Memorial One of India’s finest marble monuments and Kolkata’s most famous attraction. St. Paul’s Cathedral A magnificent Gothic cathedral dating back to 1847. Fort William The headquarters of the Eastern Command of the Indian Army, viewed from outside as public entry is restricted. Maidan Kolkata’s vast urban green space, perfect for walking and photography. Other nearby attractions include: Birla Planetarium Eden Gardens Prinsep Ghat Shaheed Minar Indian Museum Photography Photography opportunities include: Colonial grandstands Racing horses (on race days) Landscaped lawns Heritage architecture Sunset over the Maidan Panoramic views of Kolkata’s green heart Visitor Tips and Guidelines Check the race calendar before your visit. Arrive early on race days to secure good seating. Carry sun protection during warmer months. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Respect club regulations and restricted areas. Photography restrictions may apply in certain sections. Follow all instructions issued by club officials. Keep the premises clean and avoid littering. Why Visit Race Course Kolkata? The Race Course is not merely a venue for horse racing—it is a living reminder of Kolkata’s colonial legacy and sporting heritage. Its expansive green surroundings, historic grandstands, and association with the Royal Calcutta Turf Club make it a distinctive destination for history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, photographers, and sports fans alike. Whether you are attending a thrilling race meeting or simply admiring the landscape from the surrounding Maidan, the Race Course offers a unique perspective on the city’s rich cultural and historical fabric. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. What is Race Course Kolkata famous for? It is famous for thoroughbred horse racing and is home to the historic Royal Calcutta Turf Club, one of India’s oldest racing institutions. 2. When was Race Course Kolkata established? Horse racing began here in 1820, while the Royal Calcutta Turf Club was founded in 1847. 3. Where is Race Course Kolkata located? It is located in Hastings, adjacent to the Maidan and close to Victoria Memorial in central Kolkata. 4. Is the Race Course open every day? No. Public access is generally available during scheduled race meetings or special events. Access may be restricted on non-race days. 5. What is the best time to visit? October through March is the most comfortable season, with many major racing events taking place. 6. Can tourists watch horse races? Yes. Tourists can attend races by purchasing tickets for the available public enclosures during race meetings. 7. Is photography allowed? Photography is generally permitted in public areas, but restrictions may apply in certain sections or during events. 8. How do I reach the Race Course? It is easily accessible by metro (Maidan or Rabindra Sadan stations), taxi, bus, or private vehicle. 9. Which attractions are nearby? Victoria Memorial, St. Paul’s Cathedral, Fort William, Maidan, Birla Planetarium, Eden Gardens, and Prinsep Ghat are all nearby. 10. Is the Race Course suitable for families? Yes. On race days, it offers an enjoyable outing for families, sports enthusiasts, and visitors interested in Kolkata’s heritage.
